Court of Appeals Thomas opinion for audit context, without treating that excluded opinion as permissible solver material.

findings.title: Rubric requires an unsolicited reporter-pagination audit
findings.explanation: The uploaded Douglas reprint starts at printed page 313 while the Award cites 5 M.S.P.R. at 306. That discrepancy is real, but the task asks the lawyer to analyze penalty-review scope and burdens using the uploaded sources. A response could cite the reprint’s operative passage accurately and resolve every requested question without volunteering this bibliographic anomaly; the high-value criterion would fail it.

evidence.quote: State the scope of review the arbitrator was required to apply

findings.suggested_fix: Ask for a citation check expressly if it is to be graded; otherwise credit accurate use of the uploaded Douglas passage.

findings.title: Douglas places the ultimate penalty burden on the agency
findings.explanation: The criterion says no uploaded authority requires MPD to prove comparator comparability. Douglas does not use that exact phrase, but it places the ultimate burden of persuasion on the agency and requires evidence of the facts supporting penalty selection. MPD chose to rely on four purportedly similar cases. A careful lawyer could reasonably conclude that it must substantiate their similarity, while also explaining why this is not a separate categorical burden and why the arbitrator owes penalty deference. The categorical criterion may fail that qualified answer. The supplied regulation lists consistency as a factor but, by § 1600.2(g), does not itself govern sworn MPD members.

evidence.quote: the ultimate burden is upon the agency to persuade the Board of the appropriateness of the penalty imposed
the agency's obligation to present all evidence necessary to support each element of its decision
the Department did not prove that the comparator officers were similarly situated
Sworn members of the Metropolitan Police Department

authorities.citation: Douglas v. Veterans Administration, 5 M.S.P.R. 280 (1981), uploaded reprint pp. 332-33
authorities.proposition: The agency bears the ultimate burden of persuasion on penalty appropriateness and must present evidence for factual predicates of its decision.
Section 1606.2 lists consistency with same-or-similar penalties as a factor, but Chapter 16 excludes sworn MPD members.

findings.suggested_fix: Credit a reasoned allocation that recognizes Douglas’s agency penalty burden, distinguishes it from an express comparator-specific burden, and addresses the regulation’s exclusion.
